intro: Lesson 41. The teacher talks you through each section; follow the timings: A 6, B 20, C 12, D 8 minutes, then 2 minutes to check.

questions.q: Who was Duke of Milan before Antonio took over?
Who is Prospero's daughter?
Which spirit serves Prospero?
Whose island was it before Prospero arrived?
Who is Antonio's ally, the King of Naples?
Whom does Miranda fall in love with?
What does Prospero create at the start of the play?
What does Ariel want most?
What does Prospero give up at the end?
questions.a: His magic (he breaks his staff and drowns his book)

questions.q: Which value does Prospero choose over vengeance?
questions.a: Virtue, forgiveness ('The rarer action is / In virtue than in vengeance')

questions.q: How does Shakespeare present the relationship between Prospero and Ariel?
questions.a: Indicative: 'my brave spirit' (trust and pride); Ariel asks for freedom and Prospero threatens; Ariel's pity changes Prospero in Act 5; alternative: Ariel is a servant, not a friend.

passage.title: Still on Stage (extract)
paras: Every year, millions of students open a play written four centuries ago. Why? Partly because Shakespeare shaped the language we speak: phrases such as 'break the ice' and 'wild-goose chase' first appear in his plays. Partly because his stories travel: his plays have been translated into more than a hundred languages and turned into films, novels and cartoons. But mostly, it is because he understood people. Jealousy, ambition, grief and forgiveness have not changed since 1611. Reading Shakespeare is not a history lesson; it is a mirror.

questions.q: Give two reasons the writer gives for studying Shakespeare.
questions.a: Any two: he shaped our language; his stories travel; he understood people.

questions.q: What is the writer's viewpoint? Give evidence.
questions.a: Shakespeare is still valuable: 'it is a mirror'.

questions.q: Explain one method and its effect.
questions.a: The rhetorical question 'Why?' draws readers in; the list of emotions; the metaphor of a mirror.

questions.q: Link one idea to The Tempest.
questions.a: E.g. forgiveness 'has not changed since 1611': Prospero's choice still matters.
